meta.description: File census with an audit fan-out: enumerate candidates as PATHS only, one lane per file, reconcile every answer or name it missing. The 8 KB per-parent input cap, taught by example.

scan_root.desc: absolute path of the directory tree to census

audit_rule.desc: the standing rule each file is audited against, verbatim

graph.name: fan-out-audit-census
graph.description: Fan-out audit/census over a file tree. THE 8 KB CAP EXEMPLAR: a parent node's committed output is auto-injected into each child's prompt CAPPED AT 8 KB PER PARENT - content that overruns arrives truncated, so a graph that rides payload through injection is quietly corrupting its own inputs. This graph encodes the fix by shape: the census node answers FILE PATHS only (its schema pins items[].path as required - no content fields exist to overflow), each fan-out lane receives exactly one path in its item goal, reads the file itself, and answers with the path pinned back in its own schema. The parent output stays bytes-small no matter how large the tree. SEED CONTRACT (run_context map, BOTH keys required, plain text, no braces): 'scan_root' = absolute path of the directory tree to census; 'audit_rule' = the standing rule every file is judged against, verbatim. LAUNCH: run from:'general/fan-out-audit-census' run_context:{'scan_root':'/abs/path','audit_rule':'<the rule>'}. NODE MAP: census (enumerate in-scope files as a path roster, capped at 40) -> lanes (one lane per file: read, judge against the rule, answer for that path only) -> reconcile (deterministic tally from the records: every path ANSWERED or NAMED MISSING - counts computed from roster vs answers, never from prose). Read-only toward scan_root.

defaults.context: You are one lane of a file census. Ground rules: read-only toward the audited tree; judge only the file your lane owns; every claim comes from bytes you actually read; counts come from the record, never from vibes; keep the answer to the schema; one fenced json block as the final message; never print secrets.

nodes.goal: Reconcile the census. From census's committed roster (Inputs) take the expected count and path set; from your fan-out parents take the per-file answers. Every roster path must be ANSWERED or sit in missing, named by path - an honest dead lane is worth more than a shrug. Counts are COMPUTED from the two records (answered = paths answered minus dupes; missing = roster minus answered), never copied from prose. failed lists every path whose lane answered pass:false, with its finding folded into your report. verdict: clean only when missing and failed are both empty. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"expected": <int>, "answered": <int>, "missing": ["<path>"], "failed": ["<path>: <finding>"], "verdict": "clean|gaps"}
